identity: ONE original slender pale masked marsh cantor, the Sporewake veteran, facing screen right in elevated three-quarter view. Keep the ornate pale bone filigree eye-mask with an open visible mouth, the radiating crown of thin reed and bone spikes, the moss hood, the layered tan and brown shelf-mushroom shoulder mantle, the long ragged purple-mauve and moss-green robes, the bronze round chest pendant, belt bells and wrapped boots. Exactly two arms, two hands and two legs. The screen-LEFT hand holds ONE long twisted wooden crook staff upright with ONE small bell hanging inside the curl; the screen-RIGHT hand holds three fine chains supporting ONE ornate round lattice lantern with warm amber glass light and a small bell below it. Preserve the staff, the single lantern, the mask, the mantle and the slender adult proportions.
plate: Locked orthographic camera, fixed anatomical scale and centred body. Keep the full crown spikes, the staff crook, the lantern, limbs and boots within frame. The background is perfectly flat saturated BLUE throughout, no gradients or changes of hue. The blue background stays the same flat saturated blue in every frame and never darkens, flashes or changes colour. No scenery, floor shadow, camera motion, zoom, additional weapons, large magic effects, spore clouds, projectiles, particles or extra limbs; the lantern keeps only its small warm glow. Articulate joints naturally with physical planted-foot support; do not morph the staff or lantern.

idle_h3_v1.action: A solemn, swaying idle that loops. The cantor breathes, the shoulders rise and fall, the lantern is lifted a little and swings gently on its chains, the masked head tilts as if humming and the staff bell sways, then everything returns smoothly to the original stance. Both boots stay planted; the robes stir gently. No walking and no attack.

move_h3_v1.action: Walk in place through two complete reciprocal cycles with measured steps. Alternate near and far legs through forward contact, weight loading, passing and lift; both knees articulate and each boot alternates taking weight and swinging. The torso stays centred for engine-driven travel. The crook staff is planted and lifted in rhythm and the lantern swings on its chains; the robes swing with the legs. Finish in the original gait phase.

attack_h3_v1.action: Make ONE staff strike toward screen right. The cantor raises the crook staff high and back as the knees bend, then lunges and swings it forward and down so the crook reaches full extension at screen right, draws it back toward vertical, steps back and settles into the original stance. One strike only; the lantern stays hanging from the other hand and no glowing effect appears.

ranged_h3_v1.action: Release ONE spore chant toward screen right. The cantor draws the lantern in to the chest, then thrusts it out at arm's length toward screen right while singing with the mouth open as its amber light flares briefly brighter, holds a moment, then pulls the lantern back as the glow fades to ordinary and returns to the original stance. The spell itself is not shown: no spore cloud, projectile or beam.

hit_h3_v1.action: One brief impact recoil and complete recovery. The cantor hunches over as the shoulders jerk and the knees flex, keeping hold of the staff and the lantern, then straightens, rebalances on both boots and returns to the same stance. The impact is shown only by the body; the blue background never flashes or changes colour.

defend_h3_v1.action: Brace the crook staff diagonally across the front as a guard and draw the lantern tight against the chest, then duck the head behind the forearm in a deep low brace and hold it on both planted boots. No attack and no return to the relaxed stance.

cast_h3_v1.action: An invocation. The cantor raises the lantern high above the head on its chains and sings with the mouth open as its amber light glows warmer, holds it up briefly, then lowers it back to the low ready by the knee in the original stance. Only the lantern's own light changes; no aura or cloud.

death_h3_v1.action: Collapse continuously from standing: the cantor sags, sinks onto the knees with the staff slipping, falls forward onto the hands and slumps flat, finishing lying motionless face down with the crown at screen right and the boots at screen left, the staff and the lantern lying on the ground beside the body. No recovery, no floating equipment and no disappearing body.
